changes: FOUR deliverables. (1) transition-orchestrator.ts: buildPhaseTransitionProcessEvent gained optional transitionType/reason, appended only when defined, and the call site passes them only when eventType==='REOPEN' — so a gated PLAN->INIT reopen now leaves its operator-supplied reason in the append-only phase_transition event, while every normal transition keeps a byte-identical event shape. (2) Same file: the REOPEN checklist-reset comment now states its real guarantee (concurrency-atomic via the mkdir persist claim, ordered phase-write-last) instead of claiming the writes 'land together or not at all'. (3) worktree.ts: the pruneWorktreeRegistry comment now documents that `git worktree prune --expire now` cannot remove a live sibling worktree, that it is repo-wide rather than story-scoped, and that a git-worktree-locked entry survives even with its directory gone. (4) ADDED AFTER A CROSS-HOST FINDING — process-fact-registry.ts declares the reopen audit semantics (transitionType='reopen' marker + validated reason, additive, REOPEN-only, ordinary transitions omit them; declared as audit-only history, NOT gate evidence, since nothing consumes it), and scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs gained assertPhaseTransitionReopenAuditContract() which mechanically asserts all of that at the AST level. Test file plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.ts asserts the persisted JSONL carries reason + transitionType, that a refused reopen appends ZERO PLAN->INIT events, and that a real normal transition carries neither key.
usage: lattice story_advance '{"storyId":"B-xxxx","phase":"INIT","reason":"why the frozen title must change"}' from PLAN. Afterwards the reason is durably readable: reading .lattice/story/actives/B-xxxx/process-events.jsonl shows a phase_transition event with fromPhase=PLAN, toPhase=INIT, transitionType=reopen and the verbatim reason. `npm run test:process-fact-contract` now mechanically enforces those semantics.
expectedOutcome: A maintainer who reopens a story to INIT can later prove WHY it was reopened from the durable audit trail; a refused reopen leaves no event claiming success; no other transition's event shape changes; and the audit guarantee itself cannot be silently refactored away, because the process-fact contract now fails if the marker or reason is dropped.
actualTranscript: npm --prefix packages/main run build -> exit 0. node packages/main/dist/tasks/plan-init-reopen-roundtrip-smoke.js -> '✓ plan-init-reopen round-trip smoke passed' + '✓ dev_start from-main reuse + deleted-worktree re-bootstrap passed' (exit 0). node packages/main/dist/tasks/flow-stability-smoke.js -> '✓ flow stability smoke passed' (exit 0). npm run test:process-fact-contract -> 'Process fact contract verified' (exit 0). done_required_validate -> PASS: packages/main build exit 0 + root full test suite `npm test` exit 0 (586933ms). grep -c 'land together or not at all' transition-orchestrator.ts -> 0. grep -n 'live sibling' worktree.ts -> line 578. RED PROOF for deliverable 4: in isolated scratch copies, 7 distinct mutations each made test:process-fact-contract exit 1, and the primary mutation (removing the eventType==='REOPEN' call-site gate) COMPILES CLEAN while failing the contract test — independently reproduced by lattice-review-test-coverage, lattice-review-quality, and lattice-review-delivery.
outcomeDiff: The delivered scope is LARGER than originally planned, by one deliverable. Deliverables 1-3 match the original three-task request. Deliverable 4 (process-fact registration + mechanical assertion) was NOT planned: it was added after independent cross-host reviewer codex-host-b returned decision=fail with a MAJOR finding that three local Claude reviewers had passed over two rounds — the story was creating durable audit semantics with no mechanical protection against their removal, violating CLAUDE.md's dual-layer process-fact contract. Two deviations from the ORIGINAL request remain deliberate: (a) the requester's section 4 also listed actor and eventId provenance, excluded per scope-boundary.json after they answered 'no preference'; (b) their section 5 asked for stronger transition/audit-event transactionality, not added because the phase_transition event is already appended only after a successful writeStory and true crash-transactionality is a pre-existing property of ALL transitions, out of scope per their own section 6.
limitations: The audit event records reason + transitionType + fromPhase/toPhase/timestamp, but NOT actor or eventId — deliberately excluded, so the trail proves why and when a reopen happened, not which identity performed it. The event append and the phase write remain two separate fs writes under a mkdir concurrency lock: a hard crash between them can still leave a checklist reset without the phase advanced (the safe direction, since the phase write is ordered last), so this is concurrency-atomic and not crash-transactional. The registry entry is declared audit-only history, not gate evidence — no gate currently consumes transitionType or reason; the mechanical protection is the contract assertion, not a runtime gate.
pitfalls: Five things cost real time. (1) Driving lattice from a NESTED git worktree (a Claude Code worktree, not a lattice story worktree) makes INIT_CHECK's reconcile resolve a double-nested path and die with a misleading 'spawnSync git ENOENT' — git is present; the cwd does not exist. It split story metadata across two branches and required cherry-picking both code and metadata commits into the story worktree. Same bug class as B-8b69 CHK-002 but on the reconcile path. (2) The validate suite is now 51 commands and blows past story_advance's 900s watchdog (one command alone took 340s); every TEST/DONE advance needs LATTICE_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS raised. (3) Pre-writing a 'reference implementation' before dispatching implementers is a trap: independent implementers found real defects in ALL THREE reference commits, including two factually false claims about git worktree prune behavior. (4) verification_evidence_refresh_stale will rebind ANY stale evidence, including one whose recorded command was the DESTRUCTIVE 'git worktree prune --expire now -v' and one using a moving 'git diff HEAD~1' reference; both were replaced with stable non-destructive greps rather than rebound. Re-run evidence commands yourself before refreshing. (5) CLOSEOUT ORDERING: every metadata auto-commit moves materialHash, which stales verificationEvidence, delivery-check and the review-assurance floor. Update summary.json BEFORE the delivery reviewer signs (doing it after invalidates the fresh check), and bind the assurance floor LAST, immediately before story_advance DONE. The local Claude reviewer panel passed a MAJOR defect twice; only the independent cross-host round caught it — do not treat local-panel consensus as sufficient for high-assurance work.
